facts.raw_span: A 33-year-old man with no significant past medical history
presented with a 3-month history of progressively worsening occipital headache
exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers
bilateral past-pointing and an intention tremor
a 6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle
extending craniocaudally from the left ambient cistern to the premedullary space
multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas
T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components
curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci
compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem
dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles
smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, clivus, carotid canal, and foramen ovale

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a lobulated mass at the left cerebellopontine angle and smooth remodeling of the petrous apex, are consistent with a vestibular schwannoma.
The patient's imaging findings, including a mass with multiloculated cystic areas and enhancing solid components, are consistent with a meningioma.
The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle and erosion of the clivus, are consistent with a chordoma.
The patient's imaging findings, including a mass with curvilinear signal loss and corresponding T1 hyperintensity, are consistent with a hemangioma.

rationales.F04: Bilateral past-pointing and intention tremor suggest cerebellar involvement, which is more typical of vestibular schwannoma.
rationales.F05: A large lobulated mass at the cerebellopontine angle is highly suggestive of vestibular schwannoma or meningioma.
rationales.F06: Extension into the premedullary space is more typical of aggressive tumors like chordoma or meningioma.
rationales.F07: Multiloculated cystic areas are less typical of vestibular schwannoma, which usually has a more solid appearance.
rationales.F08: Enhancing solid components are seen in various tumors, including meningioma and hemangioma.
rationales.F09: Hemorrhagic foci are less typical of vestibular schwannoma, which usually does not have significant bleeding.
rationales.F10: Compression of the cerebellum and brainstem is a nonspecific finding seen in various tumors.
rationales.F11: Dilation of the ventricles suggests increased intracranial pressure, which can be seen in various tumors.
rationales.F12: Smooth remodeling and erosion of the petrous apex is more typical of chordoma or meningioma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas and T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components, along with compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem, is more consistent with a meningioma, which often presents with heterogeneous imaging features and can cause significant mass effect.
